one_line_contribution: That when a reflective prompt optimizer is run with an experience store in the loop, the resulting instruction contains machine-written clauses about how to use retrieved items, and that those clauses -- not improved task instructions -- are the causal mediator of the joint system's gain, established by annotating clauses and then deleting/transplanting them under a matched-length paired design.
closest_prior_work: Live-Evo (arXiv:2602.02369, verified on S2, 2026-02-02, 7 citations) is the nearest verified object: it runs an online experience bank alongside a meta-guideline bank, i.e. evolved natural-language text sitting above stored experience. It does not threaten the claim directly, because its guidelines are a designed second store rather than clauses an optimizer spontaneously wrote inside the task instruction, and it reports no mediation test -- but a reviewer will ask whether the proposal's 'discovery' is just Live-Evo's architecture arrived at implicitly, and the proposal itself concedes it has not read Live-Evo's full text. Two papers the proposal's own check missed are closer than it realizes. (a) 'Closing the Feedback Loop: From Experience Extraction to Insight Governance in Verbal Reinforcement Learning' (arXiv:2606.17591, verified, 2026-06-16, 4 citations) already reports the headline economics the proposal wants: the same accumulated experience either degrades performance below the zero-shot baseline or dramatically improves it depending on whether a rules-layer governance loop is present. That is 'text governing experience use is the difference between harm and gain', established on the write/curation side. (b) SelfMem (arXiv:2607.03726, verified, 2026-07-04) gives an agent memory tools and feedback and lets it explore and refine its own memory strategy -- an agent discovering rather than being handed a memory policy, which erodes the proposal's 'discovered, not hand-designed' framing even though SelfMem is conversational and does no clause-level attribution. Atlas/Compiled Memory (arXiv:2603.15666, verified, 2026-03-12) compiles experience into instruction structure, but compiles content rather than read policy, so it is a weaker threat than the brief implies. Verified but not threatening: MemTrapBench 2608.20202, Compliance Trap 2607.10608, Controllable Memory Usage 2601.05107, MemRL 2601.03192, MEMO 2603.09022, MAGE 2607.11944, Honest Lying 2605.29463, contextual drag 2602.04288, GEPA 2507.19457. I did not attempt 2603.21520 (MemAPO) or 2606.17628 (OPD-Evolver); 2609.00621 surfaced independently in my own search and exists.
strongest_objection: The study is gated on an effect its own program has already measured to be too small to decompose. The proposal fixes a minimum detectable effect of about 4 points at 300 tasks x 2 seeds and pre-registers that the joint advantage must exceed that before any mediation ratio is interpreted -- but the research brief this proposal was written against reports the measured memory gain at the 27B backbone as +0.6 points (the +7.7 figure is the 120B). The plan puts the entire confirmatory program on the 27B and uses the 120B only to swap the reflector in one ablation. The overwhelmingly likely outcome is 18,000 episodes spent to discover that the denominator of every mediation ratio is indistinguishable from zero, at which point the paper collapses into 'no joint advantage at this scale' -- a null already occupied by the archived memory_or_instruction and substitutes_not_complements ideas. A second, independent problem compounds it: P1 is close to a tautology. Read-policy clauses are defined as clauses referring to retrieved experience and how to use it, and I_solo is optimized with the store off, so I_solo structurally cannot write them. '>=20% in I_joint vs <=5% in I_solo' is therefore near-guaranteed and carries almost no information; all the load falls on P2, whose estimand is a ratio of two paired differences whose denominator sits at the noise floor. A bootstrap CI on that ratio will straddle both the 30% refutation threshold and 100%, so P2 will most likely come back uninterpretable rather than confirmed or refuted. Third, the deletion manipulation is confounded in a way length-matched filler does not fix: read-policy clauses are the only text in I_joint that refers to the injected block at all, so deleting them removes referential coherence with the context, not merely policy content -- random-clause removal is the wrong control because random clauses are not store-referential. Fourth, 'zero runtime cost' in P4 is an accounting sleight: the clauses cost a full GEPA optimization run plus prompt tokens; the honest comparison is amortized optimization cost against per-episode filtering cost, not zero against nonzero.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Move the confirmatory arms to the regime where the joint advantage is known to be large enough to decompose -- the 120B MoE, where this program measured +7.7 -- and demote the 27B to the replication, inverting the current backbone plan; or manufacture a regime with a reliably large joint gain (a deliberately noisier store, a harder task split) and say so as a pre-registered design choice. Report power for the mediation *ratio*, not only for the difference; a ratio whose 95% CI cannot exclude both 0.3 and 1.0 is not a test. (2) Replace P1 with something non-tautological: give I_solo the store during optimization but with contents replaced by length-matched filler, so both arms see a block and only one sees real experience. That single arm separates 'the optimizer reacts to retrieved content' from 'the optimizer reacts to a long unexplained block', and makes the clause-share comparison meaningful. (3) Fix the deletion control: instead of (or alongside) random-clause removal, substitute each read-policy clause with a reference-preserving, policy-destroying paraphrase (same mention of retrieved items, inverted or vacuous instruction). If deletion and scrambling do equal damage, the mechanism is referential grounding, not policy content. (4) Add a position sweep or paraphrase set for the transplant arm rather than listing position as a limitation. (5) Re-cost P4 as amortized optimizer rollouts versus per-episode filter calls. (6) Cite and differentiate arXiv:2606.17591 and arXiv:2607.03726, which the collision check missed and which a reviewer will find.
missing_baseline: A human-written read policy authored *with access to the same failure traces GEPA saw* -- one round of human reflection on the joint-arm rollouts, transplanted onto I_solo. The plan has only a 'generic hand-written read-policy sentence' (arm 5c), which is a strawman: it tests whether any boilerplate helps, not whether the optimizer's search bought anything. Without the trace-informed human policy, a confirmed P2 is fully consistent with 'a competent read policy works and GEPA was an expensive way to obtain one', which is a materially less interesting paper. Secondary omissions: an I_solo arm optimized against a filler store (separating content-reaction from block-reaction, see fix 2), and a reference-preserving scrambled-clause arm as the correct control for clause removal.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My own searches, all answered by the s2cli channel (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace; WebSearch/WebFetch unavailable per instructions, so no query used channel b): (1) --recent, 'prompt optimizer evolves instruction clauses governing how to use retrieved memory read policy agent' -> 2609.00621, 2607.04412, 2606.23664, 2606.04465, 2605.14443, 2605.00702, 2603.20667, 2603.18388, 2512.01945 (INSPO, instruction-policy co-evolution), 2508.16153; none inspects evolved instruction text for memory-use clauses. (2) 'what does the optimized prompt say about the memory clause-level analysis of evolved instructions' -> 2605.00702, 2604.08801, 2603.20667, 2505.02273, 2410.14826, 2406.15708 and older APO work; nothing on clause taxonomies of evolved agent instructions. (3) --recent, 'agent learns when to trust or ignore retrieved experience evolved guidelines meta-rules memory reliance ALFWorld' -> 2607.10608, 2606.32032, 2606.25161 (TRUSTMEM), 2606.17591 (Insight Governance -- the notable hit), 2605.29463, 2605.05583, 2601.21742, 2512.16962. (4) 'Atlas compiled memory system prompt promotion gate agent experience' -> confirmed 2603.15666 exists (initial direct id lookup returned not-found, so the proposal's citation stands). (5) --recent, 'ablating clauses from an optimized prompt to attribute the gain mediation analysis' -> only 2608.06811, 2604.25850, 2604.19821 (JTPRO), 2509.00088; the mediation-by-clause-ablation move appears genuinely unpublished. (6) --recent, 'self-discovered memory usage policy... instruction tells model when to ignore retrieved examples' -> 2607.13591 (MemCon), 2607.10608, 2607.03726 (SelfMem -- the second notable hit), 2606.05684, 2605.21463, 2603.00680, 2603.04549, 2601.05107. (7) --recent, GEPA + experience memory + ALFWorld -> 2605.10663, 2604.00901, 2603.24639, 2603.20667, 2603.18388, 2602.14697, 2601.11974, 2510.16079, 2507.19457; no GEPA-with-store 2x2 exists. Judging the proposal's own check: it is above average for this venue -- five distinct queries, IDs attached, one id verified, honest about the three WebSearch refusals rather than hiding them, and it correctly identifies Live-Evo and MemTrapBench as the nearest neighbours. But it is not exhaustive, and the two papers it missed (2606.17591, 2607.03726) both fall squarely inside its query (4) framing and both weaken the framing more than anything it did find; 2606.17591 in particular already demonstrates that a governance layer over accumulated experience is the difference between below-baseline harm and large gain. It also verified only one of the roughly twenty arXiv IDs its novelty argument leans on. I verified thirteen (2602.02369, 2608.20202, 2607.10608, 2601.05107, 2603.09022, 2607.11944, 2601.03192, 2605.29463, 2602.04288, 2603.15666, 2507.19457, 2607.03726, 2606.17591); I did not attempt 2603.21520 or 2606.17628.
